blocks.text: 这番坦白偏偏出现在公司计划于 11 月 19 日 IPO 前的最后几天，而算力只是对话中的话题之一。在与摩根大通 CEO Jamie Dimon 对谈时，他说：“算力是公司面临的最深层的商业困境。”

blocks.text: Amodei 表示，AI 技术发展太快，目前还没人知道这种进步将如何转化为经济价值。但算力必须提前一两年采购，而那时谁也不知道收入能否覆盖成本。

blocks.text: 据彭博社报道，Anthropic 已承诺投入近 9010 亿美元，其中大部分用于算力和芯片。约 710 亿美元将在 2027 年 9 月前到期。彭博社指出，这一数字超过了标普 500 指数中约三分之二公司的市值。

blocks.text: 早在 2026 年 2 月，Amodei 就以尖锐得多的措辞警告过，他可能从 2027 年底开始购买 1 万亿美元算力，一旦收入不及预期就会破产。仅仅错判一年，就可能意味着破产。他不确定一些竞争对手是否算过这笔账，并称他们并不真正理解自己承担的风险。自那以后，赌注还在不断加码。

blocks.text: Amodei 介绍了 Anthropic 缓解算力困境的两种方式：毛利率和账上现金。他说公司毛利率“相当不错”，尤其是相比其他玩家，而且 Anthropic 现金储备充足，还在寻求筹集更多资金。

inlines.text: Amodei 介绍了 Anthropic 缓解算力困境的两种方式：毛利率和账上现金。他说公司毛利率“相当不错”，尤其是相比其他玩家，而且 Anthropic 现金储备充足，还在寻求筹集更多资金。

blocks.text: 公司前期采购的算力也相对较少，如果业务好于预期，还可以转向现货市场购买额外算力。Amodei 把这种做法比作买保险：业绩不达预期时仍有保障，形势大好时又能加大投入。

blocks.text: 谈到 IPO 的时机，Amodei 语气轻松，说自己并没有盯死某个月份或某种特定的市场环境。他指出，Anthropic 从零起步，仅用六年就发展到如今的规模。他说，IPO 之前他听到最多的建议，或者说最让他有共鸣的建议，大意是“永远不要让公司的估值比它真正值的高出一美元”。他表示，这与 Anthropic 内部采用的一条准则非常相似：“少承诺，多兑现”。

blocks.text: Amodei described two ways Anthropic softens the compute dilemma: gross margins and cash on the balance sheet. He said the company’s gross margins are "quite good," especially compared with other players, and that Anthropic has a large cash balance and is seeking to raise more.

inlines.text: Amodei described two ways Anthropic softens the compute dilemma: gross margins and cash on the balance sheet. He said the company’s gross margins are "quite good," especially compared with other players, and that Anthropic has a large cash balance and is seeking to raise more.

blocks.text: The company also buys relatively little compute upfront, then can turn to the spot market for additional capacity if business goes better than expected. Amodei compared that approach to buying insurance, saying it leaves Anthropic covered if results fall short while allowing it to invest more when things go well.

blocks.text: The compute bets were the biggest reason to go public: the more cash Anthropic holds, he said, the wider its margin for error between a world with too little compute and one with too much.

blocks.text: Amodei struck a relaxed tone about the IPO's timing, saying he wasn't fixated on a specific month or particular market conditions. Anthropic, he noted, grew from nothing to its current size in just six years. The most common advice he got before the IPO, or the advice that resonated most, he said, was something like "never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's really worth." That, he said, is very similar to a model Anthropic uses internally: "under-promise and over-deliver."
